summary:
Misión Codec – Orbital Mission is an interactive educational simulator that introduces students and space enthusiasts to the planning and operation of space missions. Users begin by selecting a destination—Earth orbit, the Moon, Mars, or an asteroid encounter—and a scientific objective. In the mission design section, they build a spacecraft by choosing scientific instruments, a launch vehicle, a power system, and communication equipment. Each choice affects cost, mass, energy use, and data capacity, so players must balance the mission’s goals with a limited budget and technical constraints.

After validating their design, users launch a turn-based simulation covering launch, transit, and scientific operations. Unexpected events can affect the spacecraft, including solar particle events, radiation, micrometeoroids, communication interference, antenna faults, and low power.

The Critical Systems Control Console challenges players to interpret alerts and enter the correct commands within a time limit. Players can also practice responding to failures. At the end, a mission report summarizes the scientific score, data generated and transmitted, incidents resolved, and the effects of their decisions.

Built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, Misión Codec turns mission planning and spacecraft operations into an accessible, hands-on learning experience.
details:
Códec Misión – Misión Orbital

Misión Codec es una iniciativa educativa desarrollada para el NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. El objetivo principal de este proyecto es democratizar el acceso a la exploración espacial y a los fundamentos de la ingeniería aeroespacial para estudiantes y entusiastas mediante una plataforma interactiva que simula la planificación de misiones interplanetarias.

La aplicación funciona como un simulador de vuelo espacial que permite a los usuarios seleccionar un destino planetario, establecer una ventana de lanzamiento y configurar las especificaciones técnicas de su vehículo de lanzamiento. En función de estas entradas, el sistema determina si la nave posee el incremento de velocidad requerido (Δ v) para ejecutar la maniobra y si la fecha seleccionada constituye una ventana de lanzamiento viable. Los resultados se proyectan en un mapa bidimensional del Sistema Solar, mostrando órbitas planetarias, la trayectoria de transferencia y el tránsito simulado de la nave.

Entre las características principales de la plataforma se encuentran sus dos modos de aprendizaje distintos:

  • Modo Explorador: Diseñado para principiantes y audiencias más jóvenes, ofreciendo controles intuitivos, orientación contextual y explicaciones accesibles.
  • Modo Ingeniero: Diseñado para usuarios avanzados, permitiendo modificar parámetros técnicos como el impulso específico (\(I_{sp}\)), la masa seca, la masa del propelente y la capacidad de carga útil, mientras se presentan cálculos matemáticos paso a paso en notación científica.

Additionally, an interactive glossary has been integrated to clarify aerospace terminology and fundamental physical concepts.

The simulation engine is grounded in core principles of orbital mechanics. Kepler's equation is employed to determine planetary ephemerides and positions, Hohmann transfer equations are utilized to estimate interplanetary trajectories and transit times, and the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation is applied to calculate the change in velocity (Δ v) generated by the propulsion system. Planetary orbital elements are sourced from NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) Solar System Dynamics group. Furthermore, NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) API has been integrated to enrich the user experience with daily astronomical imagery.

From a technical standpoint, the platform was engineered using HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript, utilizing the Canvas element for the graphical rendering of the Solar System and trajectory animations. Node.js was implemented to run automated unit tests on the physics models, supported by Visual Studio Code, Git, and GitHub for version control and collaborative development. The application is hosted on GitHub Pages, ensuring universal accessibility without requiring specialized hardware. Portions of the codebase architecture were developed with artificial intelligence assistance via Claude (Anthropic).

During the design phase, critical variables were accounted for, including celestial mechanics, launch windows, propellant capacity, mass ratios, engine efficiency, and the energetic requirements for orbital transfers. To preserve pedagogical clarity, specific simplifications were established within the mathematical model: coplanar orbits, Hohmann transfers, a standardized Low Earth Orbit (LEO) ascent requirement, and a 4-degree arrival tolerance. Because the simulation models a simplified planetary flyby and does not account for orbital insertion or capture maneuvers, its outputs are intended strictly for educational purposes rather than operational mission planning.

La filosofía pedagógica de este proyecto sostiene que la educación en ciencias espaciales debe trascender la mera memorización de fórmulas. La plataforma fomenta la experimentación, el análisis de errores y la toma de decisiones basada en datos, ilustrando la complejidad de la gestión de recursos y el rigor científico requerido en la astronáutica. A través de Misión Codec, la iniciativa pretende inspirar vocaciones científicas y tecnológicas, acercando la ingeniería aeroespacial a las futuras generaciones.
